acts.14.p1.b1.text: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue, where they spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.

acts.14.p1.b2.text: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.

acts.14.p1.b3.text: So Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time there, speaking boldly for the Lord, who affirmed the message of His grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.

acts.14.p1.b4.text: The people of the city were divided. Some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.

acts.14.p2.b5.text: But when the Gentiles and Jews, together with their rulers, set out to mistreat and stone them,

acts.14.p2.b7.text: and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding region, where they continued to preach the gospel.

acts.14.p3.b8.text: In Lystra there sat a man crippled in his feet, who was lame from birth and had never walked.

acts.14.p3.b9.text: This man was listening to the words of Paul, who looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.

acts.14.p3.b11.text: And the man jumped up and began to walk.

acts.14.p4.b12.text: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices in the Lycaonian language:

acts.14.p4.b13.text: “The gods have come down to us in human form!”

acts.14.p4.b14.text: Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.

acts.14.p4.b15.text: The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates, hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds.

acts.14.p5.b16.text: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out about this, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting,

acts.14.p5.b17.text: “Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you.

acts.14.p5.b18.text: We are bringing you good news that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.

acts.14.p6.b19.text: In past generations, He let all nations go their own way.

acts.14.p6.b20.text: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven

acts.14.p6.b21.text: and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”

acts.14.p6.b22.text: Even with these words, Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them.

acts.14.p7.b23.text: Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds.

acts.14.p7.b25.text: and dragged him outside the city, presuming he was dead.

acts.14.p7.b26.text: But after the disciples had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city.

acts.14.p8.b27.text: And the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.

acts.14.p8.b28.text: They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,

acts.14.p8.b29.text: “We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God,”

acts.14.p8.b30.text: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church, praying and fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.

acts.14.p9.b31.text: After passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.

acts.14.p9.b32.text: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

acts.14.p9.b33.text: From Attalia they sailed to Antioch,

acts.14.p10.b34.text: where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had just completed.

acts.14.p10.b35.text: When they arrived, they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.

acts.14.p10.b36.text: And they spent a long time there with the disciples.
